The TMB lens: a second Laplace implementation, sampled with NUTS

Source: R/lens_tmb.R
lens_tmb.Rd

Registers glmmTMB's Laplace-approximated marginal likelihood as a lens, and samples the very TMB objective that fit produced with tmbstan's NUTS. The lens therefore contributes two things the hub's own engines do not: a Laplace implementation written independently of INLA's, and one objective sampled two ways, so a disagreement between the Laplace point and the Hamiltonian posterior is attributable to the approximation rather than to a difference of model.

Usage

lens_tmb(
  family = "gaussian",
  laplace = TRUE,
  n_draws = 2000L,
  chains = 2L,
  iter = NULL,
  warmup = NULL,
  seed = 1L,
  priors = c("hub", "flat"),
  name = NULL
)

Arguments

family

One of "gaussian", "poisson", "binomial" or "nbinom2", used when the spec is a formula. Any other family returns a family_unsupported abstention at fit time.

laplace

Logical: when TRUE (the default) the random effects stay integrated out by the Laplace approximation and NUTS samples the remaining parameters; when FALSE NUTS samples the joint vector.

n_draws

Target number of post-warmup draws in total across chains; sets the default iter when iter is NULL.

chains

Number of NUTS chains.

iter

Iterations per chain, warmup included. NULL derives it from n_draws and chains with a half-warmup split.

warmup

Warmup iterations per chain. NULL uses half of iter.

seed

Integer RNG seed passed to the sampler.

priors

"hub" to match the hub's default priors as far as glmmTMB's prior syntax allows, or "flat" to fit under glmmTMB's own defaults. See the Priors section.

name

Lens name; defaults to "tmb".

Value

A quorum_lens() with member "glmmTMB" and kind "parameters". Its fit(spec, data, ...) returns a quorum_draws() whose components are named with the hub's canonical parameters – "(Intercept)", the model-matrix column names, and sd_<grouping> – and whose diagnostics carry laplace_point (the glmmTMB point estimates on those same names), rhat (the worst-case R-hat), n_divergent, the laplace flag, and the prior plan actually used. Further arguments in ... reach tmbstan::tmbstan(). Where glmmTMB or tmbstan is not installed, the model is outside the lens's shape, or the family is unsupported, fit() returns a quorum_abstention() and never a number.

Details

The fit function accepts the model either as an lme4-style formula or as the hub's fb_terms intermediate representation, from which the formula is rebuilt the way emit_koine() rebuilds it. The lens fields a plain random intercept on one grouping variable; a random slope, a correlated structure, a nested or interaction grouping, or a second grouping term returns an out_of_scope abstention. When the spec is an fb_terms object its own family and link are authoritative, so a hub fit and this lens are never compared across two different likelihoods; a formula spec takes the family argument instead.

Priors

The hub's default is uniform(0, U) on every standard deviation, with U = 5 * sd(y) on an identity link, 3 on a log link and 5 on a logit link. glmmTMB parameterises the random-effect SD by its logarithm, so fitting with no prior at all is flat on log(SD) and thus proportional to 1/SD on the SD scale, which is not integrable at zero: for a weakly identified variance component the posterior is improper and the sampler does not settle. With priors = "hub" (the default) the lens writes a shape-2 gamma prior on the random-intercept SD. glmmTMB adds a gamma row to the negative log density as -log dgamma(exp(theta), shape, scale) with no Jacobian term, so the implied density on the SD scale is proportional to SD^(shape - 2), and shape 2 is flat; the scale is set far above the hub's bound so it stays flat across the whole interval the hub's uniform prior covers. Two parts of the hub's default have no counterpart in glmmTMB's prior syntax – the hard upper bound itself, and the uniform prior on the residual SD, since the dispersion parameter admits only log-scale families – and both are named in the fitted object's diagnostics$priors$unmatched rather than assumed away. shares["priors"] reads "hub_matched" when every hub prior on a component the lens reports (the fixed effects, which the hub leaves to the engine by default, and the random-intercept SD) was carried. With priors = "flat" the fit runs under glmmTMB's own defaults and the lens declares "flat".

See also

quorum_lens() for the contract, emit_koine() for the formula construction and the canonical naming this lens follows.

Examples

lens <- lens_tmb()
lens@shares
#>       sampler     objective        priors     data_prep 
#>   "stan_nuts"         "tmb" "hub_matched"      "quorum" 
# Outside the lens's shape, the scope gate declines rather than fits.
is_quorum_abstention(lens@scope(y ~ x + (1 + x | g)))
#> [1] TRUE
